shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Currently I have 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - a perfectly even bundle. Trading away my only A for another B would leave me with 0 A, 1 C, 2 B, which is less diverse and likely lower utility given my preference for variety. I'd rather keep balance or trade for something that increases variety, not decreases it.
Current inventory is balanced (1 each). Trading away my only B for another A would make me have 2 A and 0 B, reducing variety and utility. Not beneficial.

Trading away my only B would leave me with 0 B and 3 A, creating a highly imbalanced bundle (3A/1C/0B) despite already valuing variety. Going from 1A to 3A gives diminishing value while losing my sole B unit is costly since I'd have none left. Better to seek a trade that maintains or improves diversity, like trading C for A or a smaller quantity of B.

Current inventory is 1 each of A, C, B - perfectly balanced. Trading 1C for 1B would just shift the imbalance to C being scarce (0) while B becomes 2, without net benefit since I value variety. This trade doesn't improve my utility.

Current inventory is 1 A, 1 C, 1 B - perfectly even. Trading away B for C would just shift the imbalance to B (0) and C (2), leaving me with the same variance in holdings, no net utility gain. I'd rather keep balanced or trade to acquire a good I have zero of.

Current bundle is (A1,C1,B1). Trading away my only B for 2C would leave me (A1,C3,B0), losing variety entirely and creating heavy imbalance. Since I value variety, this trade decreases my utility rather than increasing it.

Trading away my only A (going to 0) while B goes from 1 to 2 would create an imbalanced bundle (0 A, 2 B, 1 C), which hurts my variety-based utility. I currently have equal amounts of all three goods, so giving up my sole unit of A for a good I already have is not beneficial.
Current inventory is 1A/1C/1B, perfectly balanced. Trading 1B for 1A would make it 2A/1C/0B, creating imbalance (0 of B) which reduces variety value. Not beneficial.
This trade would give me 3×A, 1×C, 0×B, creating a very unbalanced bundle with no B at all, which hurts my variety-preferring utility. I'd rather keep a more even distribution across A, C, and B.

This trade would give me 2×B and 0×C, going from an even 1/1/1 spread to an unbalanced 1/0/2. Since I value variety, moving to zero of any good decreases utility rather than increasing it. I'd rather keep my even distribution or trade for something that maintains variety.

Trading away my only B for a second C would leave me with 0 B and 2 C, reducing variety (1,2,0) rather than maintaining balance. Since I equally value all goods but prefer variety, this trade decreases my utility - I'd rather keep an even distribution than concentrate in C while losing B entirely.
Current inventory is balanced (1,1,1). Trading away my only B for 2 C would leave me with 0 B and 3 C, creating a worse imbalance since I value variety. This decreases my utility.

Currently I have A:2, C:1, B:1 - an uneven distribution. Trading away 1 A (which I have more of) for 1 B (which I have less of) moves me toward A:1, C:1, B:2, improving balance across goods and increasing my variety-weighted utility.

Current inventory is A:2, C:1, B:1. This trade would make it A:3, C:1, B:0, increasing my surplus in A (already my most held good) while eliminating my only B, which I value more due to scarcity. This decreases variety and utility, so I reject.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 1C, 2B - creating a new scarcity in A while only marginally helping variety. Current bundle is 2A,1C,1B; trading 2A away for 1B drops A to 0, which is worse for variety than the B shortage it fixes. A better trade would be 1A for 1B to balance without emptying a good entirely.

Currently I have A:2, C:1, B:1. This trade would give me A:4, C:1, B:0 - making my inventory even more skewed toward A (which I already have plenty of) while eliminating B entirely (my scarcest good along with C). This reduces variety and would hurt my utility since I value balanced holdings across all three goods.

This trade would leave me with C:0, B:2, A:2 - swapping my scarcest good (C, at 1) for another unit of B (already at 1) creates a new scarcity in C without improving variety. Current bundle A:2,C:1,B:1 is more balanced than A:2,C:0,B:2 would be.

Currently I have A:2, C:1, B:1. Trading away my only B (reducing it to 0) for a second C would make my bundle less diverse (2 A, 2 C, 0 B), which is worse under my variety-preferring utility since I'd lose a good entirely rather than balancing. I'd rather keep B at 1 and seek trades that increase my scarcest goods without zeroing any out.

Current inventory is A:2, C:1, B:1. Giving up my only extra B (down to 0) to get C up to 3 would leave me with 0 B, 3 C, 2 A - highly imbalanced and I'd have zero of a good, which hurts my variety-based utility. Better to seek a trade that doesn't zero out any good, e.g. trading A for C instead of giving away my only B.
I currently have 2 A, 1 C, 0 B. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me toward a more even distribution (A:1, C:1, B:1), which increases my utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2 A for 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 C, 1 B - trading away my entire stock of one good for less than I have of another. This over-concentrates risk and loses variety; I'd rather trade only 1 A for 1 B to balance my bundle while keeping some A.

Trading away my only C would leave me with 0 C and 1 B, just shifting the imbalance rather than improving variety. Current bundle (2 A, 1 C, 0 B) would become (2 A, 0 C, 1 B), which doesn't increase diversity - I'd still have zero of one good. Better to hold C and seek a trade for A or B without giving up my only C, or negotiate to get B while keeping C.
I currently have 0 B and 2 A, so trading 1 A for 1 B moves me toward a more balanced inventory (1 A, 3 C, 1 B), increasing variety-based utility.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0A, 3C, 1B - too concentrated in C and empty in A, which hurts my variety-based utility. A better trade would be 1A for 1B to balance my holdings without depleting A entirely.
I currently have 0 B and 3 C, so trading 1 C for 1 B improves variety, moving my bundle from (2,3,0) to (2,2,1), which is more balanced and thus higher utility given my preference for variety.

Giving up 2C for 1B would leave me with A:2, C:1, B:1 - overly depleting C from 3 to 1 while only gaining 1 B. The ratio is unfavorable; I'd rather trade 1C for 1B to balance my inventory more evenly.
Currently I have A:2, C:1, B:0 - a very unbalanced bundle. Trading 1 A for 1 B moves me to A:1, C:1, B:1, a perfectly balanced bundle, which maximizes utility given my preference for variety.
Giving up 2 A for 1 B would leave me with 0 A, 1 C, 1 B - losing all diversity in A. Better to counter for a 1:1 trade to maintain balance and variety.

I currently have C:1 and B:0, so giving up my only C would leave me with zero C while gaining B, just swapping which good I lack. This doesn't improve variety—I'd go from (2,1,0) to (2,0,1), same imbalance. I'd rather keep C and acquire B through a trade that doesn't cost me my only unit of another scarce good, e.g. trading from my more abundant A instead."}

I currently have 0 B and 3 C, so trading 1 C for 1 B improves variety balance (A:2, C:2, B:1 vs A:2, C:3, B:0), increasing overall utility given diminishing value of surplus goods.

I have 2 A, 1 C, 0 B. Trading 1 A for 1 B improves variety, moving me toward a more balanced (1,1,1) bundle, which increases utility given diminishing value of surplus goods.

Giving up 2A for 1B would leave me with 0 A, which is too costly - I'd go from a balanced (2,2,1) to (0,2,2), losing all variety in A. A fairer trade would be 1A for 1B to balance my inventory to (1,2,2).

This trade would give me 4 A, 2 C, 0 B - losing my only B entirely and creating a lopsided bundle. Since I value variety, dropping B to zero while stacking A to 4 hurts my utility more than it helps. I'd rather keep some B and seek a more balanced trade.

Currently I have 2A, 2C, 1B - B is my scarcest good. Trading 1C (I have 2) for 1B (making it 2) balances my inventory to 2A, 1C, 2B, improving variety and equalizing my holdings, which increases utility under my preference for balanced bundles.

I currently have B:1, which is my scarcest good, and C:2, which I already have relatively more of. Giving up my only B to get another C would worsen my variety balance (C would become 3, B would become 0), reducing overall utility. I'd rather keep B or trade a good I have more of.
Trading 2C for 1B would leave me with A:2, C:0, B:2 - going from balanced (2,2,1) to more skewed (2,0,2). Giving up all my C is too costly. I'd prefer a 1-for-1 trade instead.
